ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A glass plate coated with carbon black, with a mass of 2 kg, starts from rest at \( t = 0 \) and moves vertically upward with uniform acceleration under the action of a pulling force \( F \). A fixed electric tuning fork with a horizontal vibrating needle, oscillating at a frequency of 5 Hz, traces the curve shown on the glass plate. The measured lengths are \( OA = 1.5 \, \text{cm} \) and \( BC = 3.5 \, \text{cm} \).

1. How long after the glass plate starts moving does the power to the electric tuning fork begin to be connected?
2. What is the speed of the glass plate when the power is turned on? (Take \( g = 10\,\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2} \))

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is a schematic diagram of a vertically placed glass plate, on which there is an approximately sinusoidal curve left by a horizontally vibrating needle. In the middle there is a vertical equilibrium line, and the curve intersects this vertical line in sequence at four points O, A, B, and C; the problem gives the vertical distances between adjacent marks, in which OA = 1.5 cm and BC = 3.5 cm. Then reason: The tuning fork frequency f = 5 Hz, so the period T = 1/f = 0.2 s. Adjacent intersections with the center line correspond to half a period, therefore the time interval between adjacent intersections Δt = T/2 = 0.1 s. According to the specified method, regard OA as the displacement s1 of the glass plate in the first equal time interval after being energized, and regard BC as the displacement s3 in the third equal time interval. Thus s1 = 1.5 cm = 0.015 m, and s3 = 3.5 cm = 0.035 m. In uniformly accelerated motion, the displacement in the 3rd equal time interval and the displacement in the 1st equal time interval satisfy s3 - s1 = 2a(Δt)^2, so 0.035 - 0.015 = 2a(0.1)^2, giving a = 1 m/s^2. Let the speed of the glass plate at the instant of energizing be v_on, then the displacement in the first 0.1 s is s1 = v_on Δt + 1/2 a(Δt)^2, that is, 0.015 = 0.1v_on + 0.5×1×0.1^2, solving gives v_on = 0.1 m/s. The glass plate starts from rest and moves with the same acceleration until the instant of energizing, so t_on = v_on/a = 0.1/1 = 0.1 s.

method.method_draft: Read the drawing as a sinusoidal trace whose labeled points O, A, B, C are successive intersections of the trace with the vertical equilibrium line of the tuning fork needle. Since the fork frequency is 5 Hz, adjacent centerline crossings are separated by half a period, so Δt = 1/(2f) = 0.1 s. Use the measured vertical spacings from the text/image: OA = 1.5 cm and BC = 3.5 cm. Treat these as the first and third displacements of the uniformly accelerated plate in equal time intervals after the fork is switched on. For uniform acceleration, s3 - s1 = 2a(Δt)^2, so determine a. Then use s1 = v_on Δt + (1/2)a(Δt)^2 to get the plate speed at switch-on. Finally, since the plate started from rest and later has speed v_on under the same uniform acceleration, use t_on = v_on/a.

图像描述：图中玻璃板上有一条竖直中心线，顶部有向上的拉力 F 标记；调谐叉针留下的曲线在中心线附近左右摆动，并在中心线上依次标出 O、A、B、C。O 在上方边缘附近，A 在其下方，B 再下方，C 接近底部。题给测得沿竖直方向的间距为 OA = 1.5 cm，BC = 3.5 cm。

推理：按方法草稿，通电后针的水平位移可写为 x = X sin(2πft)，玻璃板竖直位移从开始描迹时刻算起为 y = v_on t + (1/2)at^2。图中 O、A、B、C 是曲线连续穿过中心竖线的位置，因此相邻点时间间隔为半个周期 τ = 1/(2f)。频率 f = 5 Hz，所以 τ = 1/(2×5) = 0.1 s。

设 O 对应 t = 0，A、B、C 分别对应 t = τ、2τ、3τ。于是 OA = y(τ)-y(0) = v_on τ + (1/2)aτ^2 = 1.5 cm = 0.015 m。BC = y(3τ)-y(2τ) = v_on τ + (1/2)a[(3τ)^2-(2τ)^2] = v_on τ + (5/2)aτ^2 = 3.5 cm = 0.035 m。

两式相减：2aτ^2 = 0.020 m。代入 τ = 0.1 s，得 2a(0.01) = 0.020，所以 a = 1 m/s^2。再代入第一式：0.1v_on + 0.5×1×0.01 = 0.015，即 0.1v_on + 0.005 = 0.015，所以 v_on = 0.1 m/s。

玻璃板从静止开始做匀加速运动，到通电时速度为 v_on，因此通电前经过时间 t_on = v_on/a = 0.1/1 = 0.1 s。

两式相减：2aτ^2 = 0.020 m。代入 τ = 0.1 s，得 2a(0.01) = 0.020，所以 a = 1 m/s^2。再代入第一式：0.1v_on + 0.5×1×0.01 = 0.015，即 0.1v_on + 0.005 = 0.015，所以 v_on = 0.1 m/s。

玻璃板从静止开始做匀加速运动，到通电时速度为 v_on，因此通电前经过时间 t_on = v_on/a = 0.1/1 = 0.1 s。

method.method_draft: Use an average-speed interpretation. From the image, OA and BC are distances covered by the glass plate during two equal-duration intervals corresponding to adjacent centerline crossings of the fork trace; each interval lasts τ = T/2 = 0.1 s. Compute the average plate speed during OA as OA/τ and during BC as BC/τ. For uniformly accelerated motion, each average speed equals the instantaneous speed at the midpoint of that interval. The midpoints of intervals OA and BC are separated by two half-periods, i.e. 2τ = 0.2 s. Use the change in these midpoint speeds over 0.2 s to find the acceleration. Then extrapolate backward by τ/2 from the midpoint speed of OA to obtain the speed at O, the moment the fork power is turned on. Finally divide that speed by the acceleration to find how long after the plate began from rest the power was connected.

Image description: The figure shows a vertical central line with an upward arrow labeled F. The sinusoidal trace made by the tuning fork crosses or meets this central line at labeled points O, A, B, and C from top to bottom. The marked vertical intervals are OA = 1.5 cm and BC = 3.5 cm. The trace indicates equal time intervals between adjacent centerline crossings because the tuning fork oscillates periodically.

Reasoning following the assigned average-speed method: The tuning fork frequency is f = 5 Hz, so its period is T = 1/f = 0.2 s. Adjacent centerline crossings are separated by half a period, so τ = T/2 = 0.1 s. Thus OA and BC are distances covered by the plate in equal intervals of 0.1 s.

Average speed during OA: v_avg,OA = 1.5 cm / 0.1 s = 15 cm/s = 0.15 m/s. For uniformly accelerated motion, this equals the instantaneous speed at the midpoint of interval OA.

Average speed during BC: v_avg,BC = 3.5 cm / 0.1 s = 35 cm/s = 0.35 m/s. This equals the instantaneous speed at the midpoint of interval BC.

The midpoints of OA and BC are separated by two half-period intervals, so Δt = 2τ = 0.2 s. Therefore the plate acceleration is a = (0.35 - 0.15) / 0.2 = 1.0 m/s^2.

The midpoint of OA is τ/2 = 0.05 s after O. Therefore the speed at O, when the tuning fork power is turned on, is v_O = 0.15 - 1.0 × 0.05 = 0.10 m/s.

Since the plate started from rest and has acceleration 1.0 m/s^2, the elapsed time before O is t = v_O/a = 0.10/1.0 = 0.10 s.

raw_record.original_question:
A glass plate coated with carbon black, with a mass of 2 kg, starts from rest at \( t = 0 \) and moves vertically upward with uniform acceleration under the action of a pulling force \( F \). A fixed electric tuning fork with a horizontal vibrating needle, oscillating at a frequency of 5 Hz, traces the curve shown on the glass plate. The measured lengths are \( OA = 1.5 \, \text{cm} \) and \( BC = 3.5 \, \text{cm} \).

1. How long after the glass plate starts moving does the power to the electric tuning fork begin to be connected?
2. What is the speed of the glass plate when the power is turned on? (Take \( g = 10\,\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2} \))
raw_record.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is a schematic diagram of a vertically placed glass plate, on which there is an approximately sinusoidal curve left by a horizontally vibrating needle. In the middle there is a vertical equilibrium line, and the curve intersects this vertical line in sequence at four points O, A, B, and C; the problem gives the vertical distances between adjacent marks, in which OA = 1.5 cm and BC = 3.5 cm. Then reason: The tuning fork frequency f = 5 Hz, so the period T = 1/f = 0.2 s. Adjacent intersections with the center line correspond to half a period, therefore the time interval between adjacent intersections Δt = T/2 = 0.1 s. According to the specified method, regard OA as the displacement s1 of the glass plate in the first equal time interval after being energized, and regard BC as the displacement s3 in the third equal time interval. Thus s1 = 1.5 cm = 0.015 m, and s3 = 3.5 cm = 0.035 m. In uniformly accelerated motion, the displacement in the 3rd equal time interval and the displacement in the 1st equal time interval satisfy s3 - s1 = 2a(Δt)^2, so 0.035 - 0.015 = 2a(0.1)^2, giving a = 1 m/s^2. Let the speed of the glass plate at the instant of energizing be v_on, then the displacement in the first 0.1 s is s1 = v_on Δt + 1/2 a(Δt)^2, that is, 0.015 = 0.1v_on + 0.5×1×0.1^2, solving gives v_on = 0.1 m/s. The glass plate starts from rest and moves with the same acceleration until the instant of energizing, so t_on = v_on/a = 0.1/1 = 0.1 s.
